overview: A single-file Python command-line tool that parses one numeric argument and prints the converted temperature, with strict input validation.

architecture.summary: One stateless component: parse, validate, convert, print.

components.name: converter
components.responsibility: Parse the CLI argument, validate it is a finite number, apply the conversion formula and print the result with two decimals.

outputs: converted temperature printed with two decimals
errors: exit code 2 with stderr message when value is not a finite number

steps: Parse the positional argument as a decimal
Print the result with two decimals
edge_cases: values below absolute zero are still converted numerically

steps: Parse the positional argument as a decimal
Print the result with two decimals
Attempt float() conversion of the argument
On failure print 'error: <argument> is not a number' to stderr
edge_cases: NaN and infinity inputs are rejected as invalid

nfr.requirement: a single conversion completes in under 50 ms

test_plan.case: temp-conv abc -> exit code 2, stderr message

tech_choices.rationale: no external dependencies for a small CLI
